handoff.purpose: Continues candidate generation for islands and shims, defines instruction builders, starts inventory_candidates function.

symbols.name: _island_instruction
symbols.note: Builds instruction string for island features. Takes name, entrypoints, tests, notes; returns a formatted string.

symbols.name: _stale_instruction
symbols.note: Builds instruction string for stale features. Takes name, entrypoints, notes; returns a formatted string.

symbols.name: inventory_candidates
symbols.note: Generates candidates from inventory structured feature entries. Returns (candidates, notes). Pure function.

claims.text: Returns ``(candidates, notes)``. Pure: takes an already-parsed inventory so the ranking is testable against a fixture with no filesystem involved.
claims.why: The function signature and return statement match; it only uses the inventory parameter and does no I/O.

claims.text: ONLY the structured feature entries are used. The top-level ``islands`` / ``stale`` arrays are prose -- one string per item, no tests, no entrypoints, no area -- which is precisely the 'no evidence' case this module refuses to queue. They are counted and reported as a note instead, so a discrepancy between the prose summary and the structured entries is VISIBLE rather than quietly resolved in favour of whichever the picker happened to read.
claims.why: The code only iterates over areas[].features[], ignoring top-level islands/stale arrays. No note generation for them is visible yet but the claim is about the design intent; the code does not contradict it.

claims.text: If unknown: Reported, never ranked: 'the engine could not classify this' is a finding about the MAP, and turning it into a work item would send a fixer to change code because a scanner was confused.
claims.why: The code appends a note about unknown modules and does not create a candidate for them.

claims.text: unnamed feature: nothing a human could act on
claims.why: The code continues to next feature if name is empty.

observations.what: Candidate generation uses many external symbols not defined in this chunk.
inventory_candidates does not handle the case where areas is a list but contains non-Mapping items; it silently skips them.
The function uses _strs, _slug, _short_hash, _spectral_row, _candidate, _map_shim_instruction, MAP_STATE_REL_PATH, INVENTORY_REL_PATH, STATUS_ISLAND, STATUS_STALE which are defined elsewhere.
